title: Bilingual Vocabulary Index (English + Gujarati)
description: Master index consolidating all themed vocabulary packs into one file. Each category holds its full word list (Gujarati meaning, Gujarati pronunciation, part of speech, difficulty, frequency, synonyms/antonyms, collocations, word forms, usage notes, memory tips, and example sentences), its mini-dialogues, and its quiz (embedded under 'quiz'). Each quiz's word_id refers to the 'id' within that same category's 'words' array. A combined all-categories flashcard deck is in vocabulary_flashcards_all.csv.

words.english_meaning: A person you know slightly, but who is not a close friend.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઓળખીતું વ્યક્તિ — જેને થોડું ઓળખો છો પણ ગાઢ મિત્ર નથી.
words.usage_note: Weaker than 'friend'. 'Make someone's acquaintance' = meet them formally.
examples: He is just an acquaintance, not a close friend.
I bumped into an old acquaintance at the airport.
She has many business acquaintances in the city.
We're mere acquaintances; we've only met twice.

words.english_meaning: To meet someone after a while and share recent news; also to reach the same level.
words.gujarati_meaning: ફરી મળીને એકબીજાના સમાચાર જાણવા; પાછળ રહી ગયેલું પૂરું કરી લેવું.
words.usage_note: 'Catch up WITH a person'; 'catch up ON work/sleep/news'.
words.memory_tip: પાછળ રહી ગયેલાને પકડી લેવું = catch up.
examples: Let's catch up over coffee this weekend.
I need to catch up on my emails.
She caught up with her college friends after years.
He stayed late to catch up on pending work.

words.english_meaning: To visit a place or person casually, usually without a fixed plan.
words.gujarati_meaning: અચાનક કે અનૌપચારિક રીતે કોઈને ત્યાં થોડી વાર માટે જવું.
words.usage_note: A short, unplanned visit. Similar: 'drop in', 'stop by'.
examples: Drop by my place whenever you're free.
She dropped by to return the book.
Feel free to drop by for a cup of tea.
He dropped by the office on his way home.

words.english_meaning: To move around and chat with different people at a social event.
words.gujarati_meaning: સમારંભમાં જુદા જુદા લોકો સાથે હળીમળીને વાતચીત કરવી.
words.usage_note: Common at parties/networking — moving from group to group.
examples: She mingled with the guests at the party.
Don't just sit there — go and mingle!
He finds it hard to mingle with strangers.
The host encouraged everyone to mingle freely.

words.english_meaning: Warm, friendly, and sincere in a polite way.
words.usage_note: Slightly formal; often used for relations or greetings.
examples: They share a cordial relationship.
She gave us a cordial welcome.
The two leaders held cordial talks.
He greeted his rival in a cordial manner.

words.english_meaning: Shared by or felt equally by two or more people.
words.gujarati_meaning: પરસ્પર — બંને પક્ષ દ્વારા સરખું અનુભવાતું કે વહેંચાતું.
words.usage_note: 'Mutual friend' = a friend you both have; 'mutual respect' = both respect each other.
examples: We have a mutual friend named Riya.
Their partnership is based on mutual respect.
The decision was reached by mutual agreement.
The feeling of dislike was mutual.

words.english_meaning: To begin to know someone, or to become familiar with something.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ સાથે ઓળખાણ કેળવવી; કંઈથી પરિચિત થવું.
words.usage_note: 'Get acquainted WITH' a person or a new place/system.
examples: Let's take some time to get acquainted.
She got acquainted with the new software quickly.
It takes a while to get acquainted with a new city.
The orientation helped new members get acquainted.

words.english_meaning: To be grateful for something; also to value or recognise it.
words.gujarati_meaning: કદર કરવી / આભારી હોવું; મૂલ્ય સમજવું.
words.usage_note: 'I'd appreciate it if you...' is a polite, indirect request.
examples: I really appreciate your help.
I'd appreciate it if you could reply soon.
She appreciates honest feedback.
We appreciate your patience during the delay.

words.english_meaning: A very polite way to ask someone to do something or to ask permission.
words.gujarati_meaning: અત્યંત નમ્રતાથી વિનંતી કે પરવાનગી માગવાની રીત.
words.usage_note: Use 'would you mind + verb-ing' or 'would you mind if I...'. A reply 'No' means 'go ahead'.
examples: Would you mind closing the window?
Would you mind if I joined you?
Would you mind helping me for a moment?
Would you mind passing me that file?

words.english_meaning: A polite, emphatic way to say 'yes, certainly' or 'please do'.
words.usage_note: A warm, willing permission. Opposite 'by no means' = certainly not.
examples: "May I see it?" "By all means."
By all means, take your time.
If you wish to leave early, by all means do.
"Can I bring a friend?" "By all means!"

words.english_meaning: A gracious reply to 'thank you', meaning you were glad to help.
words.gujarati_meaning: 'આનંદની વાત છે / ખુશીથી' — આભારના નમ્ર જવાબમાં.
words.usage_note: Warmer and more gracious than 'no problem'.
words.memory_tip: મદદ કરીને ખુશી થઈ = my pleasure.
examples: "Thanks for the ride." "My pleasure."
"Thank you so much." "It was my pleasure."
Helping you was truly my pleasure.
"We appreciate it." "My pleasure, anytime."

words.english_meaning: A formal way to apologise, or to politely ask someone to repeat something.
words.gujarati_meaning: ઔપચારિક માફી; અથવા નમ્રતાથી ફરી કહેવા વિનંતી.
words.usage_note: 'I beg your pardon?' (rising tone) = please repeat. Also signals polite surprise.
words.memory_tip: ઔપચારિક 'માફ કરજો' = I beg your pardon.
examples: I beg your pardon, could you repeat that?
I beg your pardon for the interruption.
"You're mistaken." "I beg your pardon?"
Beg your pardon, I didn't catch your name.

words.english_meaning: A polite way to express that you prefer one thing over another.
words.gujarati_meaning: 'મને... વધારે ગમશે' — પસંદગી દર્શાવવાની નમ્ર રીત.
words.usage_note: Followed by a base verb ('I'd rather stay'). 'I'd rather not' politely declines.
examples: I'd rather stay home tonight.
I'd rather have tea than coffee.
"Want to go out?" "I'd rather not."
She'd rather walk than take the bus.

words.english_meaning: A formal, slightly old-fashioned way to say 'thank you very much'.
words.gujarati_meaning: 'ખૂબ આભારી છું' — ઔપચારિક રીતે આભાર માનવાની રીત.
words.usage_note: Polite and courteous; sounds a little traditional.
examples: Much obliged for your assistance.
"Here's your coat." "Much obliged."
I'm much obliged to you for the advice.
Much obliged, sir, that was very kind.

words.english_meaning: The place where someone or something is.
words.usage_note: Noun ('his whereabouts are unknown') or casual question ('Whereabouts do you live?').
examples: Her whereabouts are still unknown.
Whereabouts in the city do you stay?
The police are tracing his whereabouts.
Do you know the whereabouts of my keys?

words.english_meaning: The area near or surrounding a particular place.
words.usage_note: Formal. 'In the vicinity of' = near.
examples: Is there a bank in the vicinity?
They live in the vicinity of the station.
All shops in the vicinity were shut.
The accident happened in the vicinity of the school.

words.english_meaning: A longer or different route taken to avoid a problem or to visit somewhere.
words.gujarati_meaning: મુખ્ય રસ્તાને બદલે લેવાતો ફરીને જતો / લાંબો રસ્તો.
words.usage_note: 'Take a detour' due to roadwork/traffic, or to see something on the way.
words.memory_tip: સીધો રસ્તો છોડી ફરીને જવું = detour.
examples: We took a detour to avoid the traffic.
There's a detour ahead because of roadwork.
Let's make a quick detour to the bakery.
The detour added an extra hour to our trip.

words.english_meaning: To move or go in a particular direction.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ દિશા તરફ આગળ વધવું / જવું.
words.usage_note: Also 'head home/out/back'; 'heading for' a place.
words.memory_tip: જે દિશામાં મોઢું (head) એ તરફ જવું = head towards.
examples: Let's head towards the exit.
I'm heading home now.
They headed for the hills at dawn.
We should head out before it gets dark.

words.english_meaning: Very near by; also means happening very soon.
words.gujarati_meaning: તદ્દન નજીક; અથવા બહુ જલદી આવનારું.
words.usage_note: Literal (very near) or figurative (very soon): 'Summer is around the corner.'
words.memory_tip: ખૂણા પાસે જ = around the corner = તદ્દન નજીક.
examples: The pharmacy is just around the corner.
Don't worry — help is around the corner.
The exams are just around the corner.
There's a lovely café around the corner.

words.english_meaning: Travelling or heading towards a particular destination.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ ચોક્કસ સ્થળ તરફ જઈ રહેલું / રવાના.
words.usage_note: Often used for vehicles/journeys: 'a flight bound for Delhi'.
examples: This train is bound for Mumbai.
They boarded a ship bound for London.
The bus bound for the airport just left.
We are bound for the mountains this weekend.

words.english_meaning: To succeed in doing or dealing with something, often something difficult.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ (મુશ્કેલ) કામ પાર પાડવું / સંભાળી લેવું.
words.usage_note: 'Manage to do' = succeed despite difficulty; 'manage without' = cope without.
examples: Somehow I managed to finish on time.
Can you manage all this work alone?
We managed without a car for a week.
She manages her time very well.

words.english_meaning: To resolve a problem or organise something properly.
words.usage_note: 'Sort out a mess/problem'; 'sort yourself out' = get organised.
examples: We need to sort out this misunderstanding.
I'll sort out the travel details.
Give me a day to sort things out.
They finally sorted out the payment issue.

words.english_meaning: To understand or solve something by thinking about it.
words.usage_note: Often 'figure out how/why/what'. Common in problem-solving.
words.memory_tip: મગજ લગાવીને સમજી લેવું = figure out.
examples: I can't figure out how this works.
Let's figure out a solution together.
She figured out the puzzle in minutes.
We're still trying to figure out what went wrong.

words.english_meaning: To move an event or task to a later time.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ કાર્યક્રમ કે કામ પાછળ ઠેલવું / મુલતવી રાખવું.
words.usage_note: Formal-ish; the informal equivalent is 'put off'.
examples: They postponed the match due to rain.
Can we postpone the meeting to Friday?
The trip was postponed indefinitely.
Don't postpone your work till tomorrow.

words.english_meaning: To change the time or date of a planned event.
words.gujarati_meaning: નક્કી કરેલા સમય/તારીખ બદલવી / ફરી ગોઠવવી.
words.usage_note: Means setting a NEW time (not just cancelling). 'Reschedule for/to Monday'.
examples: I need to reschedule our appointment.
The flight was rescheduled for tomorrow.
Can we reschedule the call to 5 pm?
She rescheduled the meeting twice.

words.english_meaning: To go out and do small everyday tasks like shopping or paying bills.
words.gujarati_meaning: રોજિંદાં નાનાં કામ (ખરીદી, બિલ ભરવું વગેરે) પતાવવા જવું.
words.usage_note: An 'errand' is a short trip to do a small task; usually used in plural.
examples: I have to run a few errands this morning.
She spent the whole day running errands.
Can you run an errand for me?
He ran some errands before the guests arrived.

words.english_meaning: To take someone or something to a place and leave them there.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈને કે કંઈને કોઈ જગ્યાએ મૂકી આવવું.
words.usage_note: The opposite of 'pick up'. 'Drop the kids off at school.'
words.memory_tip: મૂકી આવવું = drop off (≠ pick up = લેવા જવું).
examples: Can you drop me off at the station?
I'll drop off the parcel on my way.
She dropped the kids off at school.
Please drop off the keys at the front desk.

words.english_meaning: Extremely tired, with no energy left.
words.usage_note: Stronger than 'tired'. 'Exhausting' describes the cause ('an exhausting day').
examples: I'm exhausted after the long journey.
She felt completely exhausted by evening.
The marathon left him exhausted.
After a sleepless night, I was exhausted.

words.english_meaning: Feeling unable to cope because there is too much to handle or to feel.
words.gujarati_meaning: એટલું બધું થઈ જાય કે સંભાળી ન શકાય એવી લાગણી; ભારે દબાણ.
words.usage_note: From work ('overwhelmed with work') or emotion ('overwhelmed with joy').
words.memory_tip: માથે ભાર એટલો કે ઢંકાઈ જવાય = overwhelmed.
examples: She felt overwhelmed by all the responsibilities.
I'm a bit overwhelmed with work this week.
He was overwhelmed with gratitude.
The sheer amount of information was overwhelming.

words.english_meaning: Happy and satisfied with what you have; peaceful.
words.gujarati_meaning: જે છે તેમાં ખુશ અને સંતુષ્ટ; શાંત.
words.usage_note: Adjective is stressed con-TENT (satisfied); the noun CON-tent is unrelated.
examples: She is content with her simple life.
He felt content after a good meal.
They live a quiet, content life.
I'm perfectly content to stay at home.

words.english_meaning: Worried or nervous about something uncertain.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ અનિશ્ચિત વાત અંગે ચિંતિત કે બેચેન.
words.usage_note: 'Anxious ABOUT' = worried; 'anxious TO do' = eager.
examples: She was anxious about the test results.
I always feel anxious before flights.
He was anxious to hear the news.
They waited anxiously outside the room.

words.english_meaning: Feeling happy and relaxed because a worry or problem has gone.
words.gujarati_meaning: ચિંતા ટળી જતાં હળવાશ અને રાહત અનુભવવી.
words.usage_note: 'Relieved TO + verb' or 'relieved THAT...'.
examples: I was relieved to hear you're safe.
She felt relieved after the exam.
He was relieved that the storm had passed.
We were all hugely relieved by the good news.

words.english_meaning: Annoyed and discouraged because you cannot do or achieve something.
words.gujarati_meaning: ધાર્યું ન થઈ શકતાં ચીડ અને નિરાશા અનુભવવી.
words.usage_note: 'Frustrated WITH/BY'. 'Frustrating' describes the cause.
words.memory_tip: ધાર્યું ન થાય ત્યારે ચીડ = frustrated.
examples: He was frustrated with the slow internet.
She felt frustrated by the constant delays.
Don't get frustrated; just try again.
The endless traffic was really frustrating.

words.english_meaning: Extremely busy; having far too much to do.
words.gujarati_meaning: કામથી લદાયેલું; એટલું બધું કામ કે પહોંચી ન વળાય.
words.usage_note: Informal. 'Swamped with work' = buried under work.
examples: I'm swamped with work this week.
Sorry I'm late — I've been swamped.
The office is swamped during tax season.
She's completely swamped with deadlines.

words.english_meaning: At the same time; in the period between two events.
words.gujarati_meaning: એ દરમિયાન; એ જ સમય દરમ્યાન.
words.usage_note: Links two simultaneous actions or fills a gap in time.
examples: You cook; meanwhile, I'll set the table.
She read a book; meanwhile, the rain stopped.
Meanwhile, the guests were waiting outside.
He'll arrive soon. Meanwhile, have a seat.

words.english_meaning: In the end, especially after a long time, effort, or delay.
words.gujarati_meaning: આખરે; લાંબા સમય કે પ્રયત્ન પછી છેવટે.
words.usage_note: Emphasises that something happened after some time or struggle.
examples: After many tries, she eventually succeeded.
The bus eventually arrived an hour late.
He eventually agreed to come.
They eventually found the missing file.

words.english_meaning: Before a particular event; in advance.
words.usage_note: 'Do something beforehand' = ahead of time.
examples: Please let me know beforehand if you're coming.
We booked the tickets beforehand.
She prepared everything beforehand.
It's wise to plan beforehand.

words.english_meaning: During the time between two events; until something else happens.
words.gujarati_meaning: એ દરમ્યાનના સમયમાં; બીજું કંઈ થાય ત્યાં સુધી.
words.usage_note: Often used to suggest what to do while waiting.
words.memory_tip: બે ઘટના વચ્ચેનો સમય = in the meantime.
examples: The doctor will see you soon; in the meantime, please wait.
Dinner's almost ready; in the meantime, relax.
He'll call back. In the meantime, let's continue.
The repair takes a week; in the meantime, use this spare.

words.english_meaning: At some point in the future; eventually and inevitably.
words.gujarati_meaning: વહેલા-મોડા; આજે નહિ તો કાલે, પણ થશે જરૂર.
words.usage_note: Suggests something is bound to happen.
examples: Sooner or later, the truth will come out.
He'll realise his mistake sooner or later.
Sooner or later, you'll have to decide.
We all face such problems sooner or later.

words.english_meaning: For now; temporarily, until the situation changes.
words.gujarati_meaning: હાલ પૂરતું; હમણાં માટે, સ્થિતિ બદલાય ત્યાં સુધી.
words.usage_note: Signals a temporary arrangement.
examples: For the time being, we'll stay at a hotel.
This will do for the time being.
She's living with her parents for the time being.
For the time being, let's keep the plan unchanged.

mini_dialogues.title: Reconnecting with an acquaintance
mini_dialogues.situation: You unexpectedly meet someone you used to know.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: What a surprise! We haven't caught up in ages.

turns.speaker: Old acquaintance
turns.text: I know! I've been completely swamped with work lately.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Same here. Let's not stay mere acquaintances — drop by sometime.

turns.speaker: Old acquaintance
turns.text: By all means. I'd love to catch up properly.

mini_dialogues.title: Asking for directions, the polite way
mini_dialogues.situation: You stop a passer-by to find a shop nearby.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Excuse me, is there a pharmacy in the vicinity?

turns.speaker: Passer-by
turns.text: Yes, it's just around the corner, past the bank.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The main road is jammed — could I take a detour?

turns.speaker: Passer-by
turns.text: Sure, head towards the park and turn left.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Much obliged for your help.

mini_dialogues.title: Rescheduling politely
mini_dialogues.situation: You need to move a meeting to another day.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm afraid I need to reschedule our meeting.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: No problem. Would you mind moving it to Friday?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'd rather make it Monday, if that works for you.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: By all means. In the meantime, I'll sort out the documents.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I really appreciate your flexibility.

mini_dialogues.title: A stressful day
mini_dialogues.situation: A friend notices you're not yourself.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: You look exhausted. Is everything okay?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Honestly, I'm a bit overwhelmed — I've got so much to manage.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: I get frustrated on days like that too.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thanks for asking. I feel relieved just talking about it.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Take a break. You'll sort it out eventually.

mini_dialogues.title: Dividing the chores
mini_dialogues.situation: You and a family member plan before guests arrive.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I have to run a few errands before the guests arrive.

turns.speaker: Family member
turns.text: Would you mind dropping off this parcel on the way?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: By all means. I'll head towards the post office first.

turns.speaker: Family member
turns.text: Great. Meanwhile, I'll get the house ready.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Perfect. Let me know beforehand if you need anything else.

words.english_meaning: The central part of a city, especially its main business area.
words.usage_note: American-style term; also an adverb ('go downtown'). UK often says 'city centre'.
examples: She works downtown in a tall office building.
Let's go downtown for dinner tonight.
The downtown area is full of shops and offices.
Traffic is heavy downtown during rush hour.

words.english_meaning: A residential area on the edge of a city, away from the centre.
words.usage_note: Often plural, 'the suburbs'. Adjective: 'suburban'.
examples: They moved to a quiet suburb last year.
Life in the suburbs is calmer than downtown.
The suburb has good schools and parks.
He commutes from the suburb to the city daily.

words.english_meaning: The outer parts of a town or city, far from the centre.
words.gujarati_meaning: શહેર કે ગામની બહારની હદ / છેવાડાનો વિસ્તાર.
words.usage_note: Always plural; usually 'on the outskirts of'.
examples: Their farm is on the outskirts of the city.
The airport lies on the outskirts of town.
Rents are cheaper on the outskirts.
We drove to the outskirts to escape the noise.

words.english_meaning: A district or area within a town, and the people who live there.
words.usage_note: Refers to both the place and its community. (US spelling: 'neighborhood'.)
examples: We live in a friendly neighbourhood.
There's a new café in the neighbourhood.
The whole neighbourhood came to the festival.
It's a safe neighbourhood for children.

words.english_meaning: A particular area or district of a town or region.
words.usage_note: Slightly formal; common in Indian English for a residential area.
examples: Many old families live in this locality.
Is there a hospital in the locality?
The locality is known for its temples.
Property prices in this locality have risen.

words.english_meaning: A very large, busy, and important city.
words.usage_note: Formal/literary. Adjective: 'metropolitan'.
examples: Mumbai is a bustling metropolis.
The quiet town grew into a metropolis.
Living in a metropolis can be exhausting.
The metropolis never seems to sleep.

words.english_meaning: An area made up mainly of houses, where people live (not shops or factories).
words.usage_note: Contrasted with 'commercial' or 'industrial' areas.
examples: They built a school in the residential area.
It's a quiet residential area with little traffic.
Shops are not allowed in this residential area.
The residential area is surrounded by gardens.

words.english_meaning: A building together with its land and surroundings, used by a business or person.
words.gujarati_meaning: મકાન અને તેની જમીન / મિલકતનો વિસ્તાર.
words.usage_note: Always plural in this sense. 'On the premises' = inside the building/grounds.
examples: Smoking is not allowed on the premises.
The company moved to larger premises.
Security guards patrol the premises at night.
Customers must leave the premises by ten.

words.english_meaning: A large entrance hall inside a hotel, office, or public building.
words.usage_note: The first area you enter; often has reception and seating.
examples: Let's meet in the hotel lobby at nine.
The lobby was decorated with fresh flowers.
She waited in the lobby for her appointment.
The office lobby has comfortable sofas.

words.english_meaning: An entrance area or small lobby just inside the doors of a building, theatre, or home.
words.usage_note: Often used for theatres/cinemas/large homes. (French; said 'FOY-ay'.)
examples: We met in the theatre foyer during the interval.
Guests gathered in the foyer before dinner.
The foyer leads into the main hall.
Leave your umbrella in the foyer.

words.english_meaning: A long passage inside a building, with rooms opening off it.
words.usage_note: Connects rooms within a building (school, hospital, hotel).
examples: Her office is at the end of the corridor.
Students lined up in the corridor.
The hotel corridor was long and quiet.
We walked down the corridor to the exit.

words.english_meaning: A floor of a building that is partly or completely below ground level.
words.usage_note: Often used for storage or parking.
examples: The car park is in the basement.
We store old boxes in the basement.
The basement stays cool in summer.
There's a gym in the building's basement.

words.english_meaning: An open, flat area on the roof of a building, or a raised paved area beside it.
words.usage_note: In Indian English often the rooftop; can also be a paved outdoor area.
examples: We had dinner on the terrace under the stars.
Children fly kites on the terrace.
The café has a lovely rooftop terrace.
She grows plants on her terrace.

words.english_meaning: An open area surrounded by walls or buildings, usually within or beside a building.
words.gujarati_meaning: મકાનની વચ્ચે દીવાલોથી ઘેરાયેલું ખુલ્લું આંગણું.
words.usage_note: Common in old houses, palaces, schools — an enclosed open space.
examples: The old house has a central courtyard.
Children played in the courtyard.
A fountain stood in the middle of the courtyard.
The temple's courtyard was full of pilgrims.

words.english_meaning: A building where journeys by air, bus, or sea begin and end.
words.gujarati_meaning: જ્યાં મુસાફરી શરૂ/પૂરી થાય તે મથક (એરપોર્ટ/બસ).
words.usage_note: Airports have several terminals; also 'bus terminal'.
words.memory_tip: મુસાફરી શરૂ/પૂરી થાય તે મથક = terminal.
examples: Our flight leaves from Terminal 2.
The bus terminal was crowded with travellers.
Check which terminal your airline uses.
We waited at the terminal for two hours.

words.english_meaning: A place where two or more roads or railway lines meet.
words.gujarati_meaning: જ્યાં રસ્તા કે રેલમાર્ગ મળે તે સ્થળ / સંગમ.
words.usage_note: For roads (intersection) or railways (a major station where lines meet).
examples: Turn right at the next junction.
It's a major railway junction.
There was an accident at the busy junction.
The two highways meet at this junction.

words.english_meaning: The raised area beside the track at a station where you get on or off a train.
words.gujarati_meaning: સ્ટેશન પર ગાડી પકડવા માટેનો ઉંચો ઓટલો / પ્લેટફોર્મ.
words.usage_note: Trains arrive 'at' a platform; e.g. 'platform 4'.
words.memory_tip: સ્ટેશન પર ગાડી પકડવાનો ઓટલો = platform.
examples: The train arrives at platform three.
We waited on the platform in the cold.
Mind the gap between the train and the platform.
Passengers crowded the platform at rush hour.

words.english_meaning: A place where buses, trains, or goods are kept, parked, or stored.
words.usage_note: For storage or for parking/maintaining vehicles. (Said 'DEE-poh'.)
examples: The buses return to the depot at night.
Goods are stored at the railway depot.
He works as a mechanic at the bus depot.
The depot houses over a hundred buses.

words.english_meaning: A small house or place to stay, often in the countryside or at the entrance to an estate.
words.gujarati_meaning: રહેવા માટેનું નાનું મકાન (ખાસ ગ્રામ્ય વિસ્તારમાં).
words.usage_note: Often a holiday/rest place in nature; also a gatekeeper's small house.
words.memory_tip: ગ્રામ્ય વિસ્તારમાં રહેવાનું નાનું મકાન = lodge.
examples: We stayed in a cosy lodge in the hills.
The safari lodge overlooked a river.
A ski lodge stood at the foot of the mountain.
The guard lives in the lodge by the gate.

words.english_meaning: A place providing cheap accommodation, especially for students or travellers.
words.usage_note: Budget lodging with shared facilities; common for students/backpackers.
examples: Backpackers often stay in a hostel.
She lives in a student hostel near campus.
The youth hostel was clean and cheap.
We booked a hostel for the weekend trip.

words.english_meaning: A shop where medicines are prepared and sold.
words.usage_note: UK 'chemist's', US 'drugstore'. The person is a 'pharmacist'.
examples: I bought the medicine from the pharmacy.
Is there a pharmacy open at night?
The pharmacy is next to the clinic.
The pharmacist explained how to take the tablets.

words.english_meaning: A small open-fronted stall or booth where things are sold or information is given.
words.gujarati_meaning: નાનો સ્ટોલ / કેબિન જ્યાં વસ્તુ વેચાય.
words.usage_note: Small, often standalone; sells newspapers, snacks, tickets, etc.
examples: I bought a magazine from the kiosk.
There's a ticket kiosk near the gate.
The kiosk sells snacks and cold drinks.
She runs a small kiosk at the station.

words.english_meaning: A shop or store, especially one that sells a particular brand's goods.
words.usage_note: 'Factory outlet' sells at lower prices; 'retail outlet' = a shop.
examples: There's a new outlet of that brand in the mall.
We bought shoes at the factory outlet.
The company has outlets across the country.
This outlet offers great discounts.

words.english_meaning: A local office or shop that is part of a larger company or organisation.
words.usage_note: 'Head office' is the main one; 'branches' are the local ones.
examples: I opened an account at the local bank branch.
The store has branches in every city.
Our nearest branch is on Main Street.
She manages the branch office downtown.

words.english_meaning: A large building where goods are stored before being sold or sent out.
words.usage_note: In Indian English, 'godown' is a common equivalent.
examples: The goods are kept in a large warehouse.
Workers loaded boxes onto trucks at the warehouse.
The warehouse stores furniture and appliances.
Online orders are shipped from this warehouse.

words.english_meaning: A small shop selling fashionable clothes or accessories.
words.usage_note: Implies small, stylish, often expensive. (French; said 'boo-TEEK'.)
examples: She bought a dress from a designer boutique.
A new boutique opened in the market.
The boutique sells handmade jewellery.
Prices at the boutique are quite high.

words.english_meaning: A shop that sells food and small household goods.
words.usage_note: 'The grocer's' = the shop; 'grocer' = the shopkeeper. US: 'grocery store'.
examples: I'm going to the grocer's for some milk.
The grocer's on the corner stays open late.
She buys vegetables from the local grocer's.
We ran out of sugar, so I went to the grocer's.

words.english_meaning: Full of busy, lively activity and lots of people.
words.usage_note: Positive: energetic and full of life.
examples: The market was bustling with shoppers.
She loves the bustling streets of the old city.
It's a bustling town full of energy.
The station was bustling during the festival.

words.english_meaning: Attractively old-fashioned in an unusual and charming way.
words.usage_note: Positive — pleasantly old-fashioned (cottages, villages, lanes).
examples: They stayed in a quaint little village.
The town is full of quaint old cottages.
We browsed the quaint shops along the lane.
It's a quaint café with vintage decor.

words.english_meaning: Visually attractive, like a picture; charming scenery.
words.usage_note: Usually about places/scenery that look beautiful.
examples: The village sits in a picturesque valley.
We drove along a picturesque coastal road.
The lake offers picturesque views.
It's a picturesque spot for photos.

words.english_meaning: Private and quiet; far away from other people.
words.usage_note: Often positive — peaceful privacy.
examples: We found a secluded beach with no crowds.
Their house is in a secluded part of the hills.
She enjoys the secluded garden behind her home.
It's a secluded spot, perfect for reading.

words.english_meaning: In poor condition because of neglect; old and shabby.
words.usage_note: Negative — neglected and in disrepair.
examples: They bought a run-down house and repaired it.
The factory was old and run-down.
It used to be a run-down area, now it's modern.
The hotel looked run-down and dirty.

words.english_meaning: Having plenty of space; large and roomy.
words.usage_note: Positive — comfortably large.
examples: The new flat is bright and spacious.
They have a spacious living room.
The hall was spacious enough for 200 guests.
I prefer a spacious office to a cramped one.

words.english_meaning: Empty, with no people present.
words.usage_note: Means temporarily empty or abandoned of people.
examples: The streets were deserted late at night.
We found a deserted beach.
The old village is now completely deserted.
At noon the office looked deserted.

words.english_meaning: A very short distance away; very close.
words.usage_note: Informal idiom for 'very near'.
examples: The beach is just a stone's throw away from our hotel.
The school is a stone's throw away from home.
Shops are a stone's throw away.
It's only a stone's throw from the station.

words.english_meaning: In a remote, quiet place away from popular or busy routes.
words.gujarati_meaning: મુખ્ય રસ્તાથી દૂર, અજાણ્યું એકાંત સ્થળ.
words.usage_note: Idiom; often positive for travellers wanting quiet, unusual spots.
words.memory_tip: મુખ્ય રસ્તાથી દૂરનું = off the beaten track.
examples: We like holidays off the beaten track.
The village is off the beaten track and very peaceful.
For real adventure, go off the beaten track.
This café is off the beaten track but worth finding.

words.english_meaning: In the very centre or most important part of a place.
collocations: in the heart of the city
words.usage_note: Emphasises a central, lively location.
words.memory_tip: બરાબર મધ્યમાં = in the heart of.
examples: The hotel is in the heart of the city.
Their shop is in the heart of the market.
We stayed in the heart of the old town.
The park lies in the heart of the campus.

words.english_meaning: Close enough to be reached easily on foot.
words.usage_note: Use 'within walking distance OF' a place.
words.memory_tip: ચાલીને પહોંચાય એટલું નજીક = within walking distance.
examples: The market is within walking distance of my house.
Everything we need is within walking distance.
The office is within walking distance from the station.
We chose a hotel within walking distance of the beach.

words.english_meaning: Very far from any town or other people; extremely remote.
words.usage_note: Informal; emphasises isolation.
words.memory_tip: દરેક વસ્તીથી દૂર = miles from anywhere.
examples: Their farmhouse is miles from anywhere.
We broke down miles from anywhere.
The resort felt miles from anywhere, totally peaceful.
It's a lonely cottage, miles from anywhere.

words.english_meaning: Very close to where you live or are; right nearby.
words.usage_note: Idiom — so near it's almost at your door. Often 'right on the doorstep'.
words.memory_tip: બારણા આગળ જ = on the doorstep.
examples: We have a beautiful park right on our doorstep.
The beach is on our doorstep.
Good schools are on the doorstep here.
With the station on the doorstep, commuting is easy.

mini_dialogues.title: Describing where you live
mini_dialogues.situation: A new colleague asks about your area.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: What's the neighbourhood like where you live?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: It's a quiet residential area on the outskirts of town.

turns.speaker: Colleague
turns.text: Isn't that far from downtown?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Not really — the metro is within walking distance.

mini_dialogues.title: At the railway station
mini_dialogues.situation: You need to find your train and a snack.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Excuse me, which platform is the train to Pune?

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: Platform four. It's a major junction, so check the board.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Is there somewhere to grab a snack?

turns.speaker: Staff
turns.text: There's a kiosk near the terminal entrance.

mini_dialogues.title: Talking about a holiday spot
mini_dialogues.situation: A friend asks about your trip to the hills.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: How was the hill station?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Picturesque and wonderfully secluded — really off the beaten track.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Wasn't it too remote?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: A bit — it felt miles from anywhere, but that was the charm.

mini_dialogues.title: Renting a shop space
mini_dialogues.situation: You're looking for a place to open a business.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm looking for premises to open a boutique.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: There's a spacious outlet in the heart of the market.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Is it in good condition?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Yes, freshly renovated — not run-down at all.

mini_dialogues.title: Finding your house
mini_dialogues.situation: You explain how easy your home is to find.

turns.speaker: Guest
turns.text: Where exactly is your place?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: In a lovely old locality, full of quaint little houses.

turns.speaker: Guest
turns.text: Easy to find?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Very — there's a pharmacy right on the doorstep, you can't miss it.

words.english_meaning: A short trip taken for pleasure.
words.gujarati_meaning: મોજમજા માટેની ટૂંકી સહેલ / ફરવા જવાનું.
words.usage_note: A pleasure trip, usually for a day or less.
examples: We went on a family outing to the lake.
The school organised an outing to the zoo.
A weekend outing is a great way to relax.
Pack some snacks for the outing.

words.english_meaning: A short holiday taken to escape from everyday life.
words.gujarati_meaning: રોજિંદી ભાગદોડથી દૂર ટૂંકું વેકેશન / છૂટકારો.
words.usage_note: Informal; suggests a relaxing short escape.
examples: We booked a weekend getaway to the hills.
A short getaway can refresh your mind.
They planned a quiet getaway by the sea.
The resort is perfect for a quick getaway.

words.english_meaning: A short organised trip, often in a group, for leisure or learning.
words.usage_note: Slightly formal; often a planned or guided group trip.
examples: The hotel offers excursions to nearby villages.
We took a boat excursion along the coast.
The class went on an excursion to the museum.
A guided excursion made the trip easier.

words.english_meaning: A journey to a place and back again on the same day.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક જ દિવસમાં પૂરી થતી સફર.
words.usage_note: No overnight stay — you return the same day.
examples: We took a day trip to the beach.
It's an easy day trip from the city.
They went on a day trip to the old fort.
A day trip needs less packing than a holiday.

words.english_meaning: A planned route or schedule for a journey or trip.
words.usage_note: Formal; the day-by-day plan of a trip. (Said 'eye-TIN-er-ree'.)
examples: Our itinerary includes three cities in five days.
She prepared a detailed itinerary for the tour.
Check the itinerary before you pack.
The guide handed us the day's itinerary.

words.english_meaning: The place where an event or activity happens.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ કાર્યક્રમ / મેળાવડો યોજાય તે સ્થળ.
words.usage_note: Used for events — parties, picnics, concerts, meetings.
examples: The park is a great venue for a picnic.
They booked a riverside venue for the party.
The venue was changed due to rain.
We chose a shady venue for the gathering.

words.english_meaning: An event where a group of people come together.
words.usage_note: Any event where people meet — informal or formal.
examples: We had a small family gathering in the garden.
The picnic turned into a happy gathering.
It was a quiet gathering of close friends.
Such gatherings bring everyone together.

words.english_meaning: A basket, usually with a lid, packed with food for a picnic.
words.gujarati_meaning: પિકનિક માટે ખાવાનું ભરેલી ઢાંકણાવાળી ટોપલી.
words.usage_note: A picnic hamper holds food; a 'gift hamper' is a basket of gifts.
examples: She packed sandwiches into the picnic hamper.
We carried a hamper full of treats.
The hamper had a flask and some fruit.
They received a lovely gift hamper.

words.english_meaning: A blanket or mat spread on the ground to sit on during a picnic.
words.gujarati_meaning: જમીન પર બેસવા માટેનું પાથરણું / ચાદર.
words.usage_note: British term; 'rug' here means a thick blanket for sitting outdoors.
examples: We spread the picnic rug under a tree.
Everyone sat on the picnic rug to eat.
Don't forget the picnic rug for the grass.
The rug kept us off the damp ground.

words.english_meaning: A container that keeps drinks hot or cold for a long time.
words.gujarati_meaning: પીણું ગરમ કે ઠંડું રાખવાનું પાત્ર / થર્મોસ.
words.usage_note: A 'flask' (or 'thermos') keeps tea/coffee hot on outings.
examples: I filled a flask with hot tea for the trip.
Keep the coffee in a flask to stay warm.
She poured soup from the flask.
A cold-water flask is useful in summer.

words.english_meaning: Knives, forks, and spoons used for eating.
words.gujarati_meaning: છરી, કાંટો, ચમચી વગેરે જમવાનાં સાધનો.
words.usage_note: Uncountable; 'a piece of cutlery'. For picnics, often disposable.
examples: Pack some cutlery for the picnic.
We used plastic cutlery to save washing up.
The cutlery was wrapped in napkins.
Don't forget spoons in the cutlery set.

words.english_meaning: Light food and drinks served at an event or during a trip.
words.usage_note: Usually plural; light snacks/drinks rather than a full meal.
examples: Light refreshments were served at the picnic.
We packed plenty of refreshments.
Refreshments will be available at the venue.
After the hike, we stopped for refreshments.

words.english_meaning: Food that remains uneaten after a meal.
words.usage_note: Usually plural. 'Leftover' (adj) before a noun: 'leftover cake'.
examples: We packed the leftovers to take home.
There were plenty of leftovers after lunch.
Don't waste the leftovers — save them.
We had leftover sandwiches on the journey back.

words.english_meaning: Made to be thrown away after one use.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક વાર વાપરીને ફેંકી દેવાય એવું.
words.usage_note: Adjective ('disposable plates'); handy for picnics but less eco-friendly.
examples: We used disposable plates at the picnic.
Disposable cups save washing up.
Try to avoid too much disposable plastic.
They brought disposable cutlery for everyone.

words.english_meaning: A field covered with grass and wildflowers.
words.usage_note: A pretty, literary word for an open grassy field.
examples: We had our picnic in a flower-filled meadow.
Cows grazed in the green meadow.
The meadow was bright with wildflowers.
Children ran freely across the meadow.

words.english_meaning: The land along the edge of a river.
words.usage_note: A popular picnic spot; 'on/along the riverbank'.
examples: We sat on the riverbank and ate lunch.
A path runs along the riverbank.
They fished from the grassy riverbank.
The riverbank was shaded by tall trees.

words.english_meaning: An open space in a wood or forest with no trees.
words.usage_note: A natural open patch among trees — good for resting.
examples: We set up the picnic in a sunny clearing.
Deer often visit the forest clearing.
A small clearing opened up among the trees.
They camped in a grassy clearing.

words.english_meaning: An area sheltered from direct sunlight.
words.usage_note: 'In the shade' = out of the sun. Adjective: 'shady'.
examples: We sat in the shade of a big tree.
Find some shade — it's too hot here.
The umbrella gave us welcome shade.
Children played in the shade all afternoon.

words.english_meaning: An area of short, mown grass, especially in a garden or park.
words.usage_note: Mown grass in gardens/parks — a common picnic surface.
examples: We laid the rug on the soft lawn.
The park has a wide green lawn.
Children rolled on the lawn.
We had tea on the lawn behind the house.

words.english_meaning: A small group of trees.
words.usage_note: Often named by tree type: 'mango grove', 'orange grove'.
examples: We rested in a cool mango grove.
The grove offered plenty of shade.
Birds sang in the orange grove.
A small grove stood beside the field.

words.english_meaning: A path or track through the countryside or a natural area.
words.gujarati_meaning: કુદરત વચ્ચેથી પસાર થતી પગદંડી / કેડી.
words.usage_note: A marked path for walking/hiking in nature.
examples: We followed a nature trail through the woods.
The hiking trail leads to a waterfall.
Stay on the trail so you don't get lost.
The trail was lined with wildflowers.

words.english_meaning: To walk in a slow, relaxed way; a leisurely walk.
words.usage_note: Both verb and noun; a relaxed, unhurried walk.
examples: We went for a stroll along the river.
An evening stroll helps me relax.
They strolled through the park hand in hand.
After lunch, we took a slow stroll.

words.english_meaning: To walk around in a relaxed way without a fixed route or purpose.
words.gujarati_meaning: કોઈ નક્કી માર્ગ વગર આમતેમ ફરવું.
words.usage_note: 'Wander around' = explore aimlessly; 'wander off' = stray away.
examples: We wandered around the old town for hours.
Don't wander off too far from the group.
They wandered through the gardens.
I love to wander with no plan.

words.english_meaning: The activity of visiting interesting places, especially as a tourist.
words.usage_note: Usually 'go sightseeing'; visiting attractions.
examples: We spent the morning sightseeing in the city.
A sightseeing tour covered all the main spots.
After the picnic, we went sightseeing.
There's plenty of sightseeing to do here.

words.english_meaning: To relax and stop feeling anxious or tense.
words.gujarati_meaning: તણાવ ભૂલીને હળવા થવું / આરામ કરવો.
words.usage_note: To release stress; a getaway is a good way to unwind.
examples: A day in nature helps me unwind.
We went to the lake to unwind.
She unwinds by reading in the garden.
Picnics are a lovely way to unwind.

words.english_meaning: An outdoor meal where food is cooked over a fire or grill; also the grill itself.
words.gujarati_meaning: ખુલ્લામાં શેકીને જમવાનો કાર્યક્રમ / શેકેલું ભોજન.
words.usage_note: Both the event and the cooking equipment. Short form: 'BBQ'.
examples: We had a barbecue in the backyard.
They grilled vegetables on the barbecue.
A barbecue is perfect for a summer outing.
The smell of the barbecue filled the air.

words.english_meaning: A long walk in the countryside or mountains, for pleasure or exercise.
words.usage_note: Longer and more energetic than a stroll; done in nature.
examples: We went for a hike up the hill.
The hike offered stunning views.
Wear good shoes for the long hike.
After the hike, we rested in the shade.

words.english_meaning: To sit or lie in a relaxed, lazy way.
words.usage_note: As a verb = relax lazily; (also a noun meaning a sitting room).
examples: We lounged on the grass after lunch.
They spent the afternoon lounging by the pool.
I love to lounge in the shade with a book.
We just lounged around and did nothing.

words.english_meaning: (Of the sky) covered with grey clouds; dull and cloudy.
words.usage_note: Describes a fully cloudy sky (but not necessarily raining).
examples: The sky was overcast, so we took umbrellas.
It stayed overcast all afternoon.
An overcast day kept the picnic cool.
Despite the overcast sky, we had fun.

words.english_meaning: A gentle, light wind.
words.usage_note: A pleasant light wind. Adjective: 'breezy'.
examples: A cool breeze made the picnic pleasant.
We enjoyed the gentle breeze by the river.
The sea breeze felt refreshing.
Leaves rustled in the soft breeze.

words.english_meaning: Light rain made of very fine drops.
words.usage_note: Both noun and verb; gentle, fine rain.
examples: A light drizzle began as we ate.
We carried on despite the drizzle.
It started to drizzle in the afternoon.
The drizzle soon stopped and the sun came out.

words.english_meaning: Extremely hot.
words.gujarati_meaning: અતિશય ગરમ, બાળી નાખે એવો તડકો.
words.usage_note: A strong word for very hot weather.
examples: It was a scorching day, so we stayed in the shade.
We avoided the scorching afternoon sun.
The scorching heat made us thirsty.
Carry water on a scorching day.

words.english_meaning: (Of air or weather) damp and sticky, with a lot of moisture.
words.usage_note: Often paired with 'hot and humid'. Noun: 'humidity'.
examples: The weather was hot and humid.
It felt humid before the rain.
A humid afternoon left us sweaty.
The coast is very humid in summer.

words.english_meaning: Enjoyable, nice, and agreeable.
words.usage_note: Common for mild, comfortable weather or a nice time.
examples: The weather was pleasant for a picnic.
We had a pleasant afternoon by the lake.
A pleasant breeze cooled the air.
It was a pleasant change from the city heat.

words.english_meaning: Outdoors; in the fresh air rather than inside a building.
words.usage_note: Emphasises being outside in fresh air.
words.memory_tip: ખુલ્લી હવામાં = in the open air.
examples: Eating in the open air feels wonderful.
We slept in the open air under the stars.
The concert was held in the open air.
There's nothing like exercise in the open air.

words.english_meaning: To use or enjoy something as much as possible.
collocations: make the most of the day
words.usage_note: Idiom — get the maximum benefit or enjoyment.
words.memory_tip: પૂરેપૂરો લાભ લેવો = make the most of.
examples: Let's make the most of this sunny day.
We made the most of our short holiday.
Make the most of your time outdoors.
They made the most of the long weekend.

words.english_meaning: A new and different environment that makes you feel refreshed.
words.usage_note: Idiom — going somewhere different for a refreshing break.
words.memory_tip: સ્થળ બદલવાથી તાજગી = a change of scenery.
examples: A picnic gives us a nice change of scenery.
I needed a change of scenery after a busy week.
The countryside was a welcome change of scenery.
Sometimes a change of scenery lifts your mood.

words.english_meaning: So perfect and beautiful that it looks like a picture.
words.gujarati_meaning: ચિત્ર જેવું તદ્દન સંપૂર્ણ અને સુંદર.
words.usage_note: Strongly positive — ideal and lovely.
examples: We found a picture-perfect spot for the picnic.
The weather was picture-perfect.
It was a picture-perfect day by the sea.
The valley looked picture-perfect at sunset.

words.english_meaning: Relaxed and easy-going; not worried or in a hurry.
words.usage_note: Describes a relaxed mood, person, or atmosphere.
examples: The picnic had a lovely laid-back feel.
He has a very laid-back attitude.
We spent a laid-back afternoon by the river.
It was a laid-back gathering with no rush.

words.english_meaning: So beautiful or impressive that it amazes you.
words.gujarati_meaning: શ્વાસ થંભાવી દે એવું અતિ સુંદર / અદ્ભુત.
words.usage_note: Strongly positive — for stunning views or scenery.
words.memory_tip: શ્વાસ થંભાવી દે એવું સુંદર = breathtaking.
examples: The view from the hilltop was breathtaking.
We enjoyed breathtaking scenery on the trail.
The sunset over the sea was breathtaking.
It's a breathtaking spot for a picnic.

mini_dialogues.title: Planning the picnic
mini_dialogues.situation: Two friends plan a weekend outing.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Shall we go on a picnic this weekend?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Yes! Let's plan a day trip to the meadow on the riverbank.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'll prepare the itinerary and pack the hamper.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Great — let's make the most of the good weather.

mini_dialogues.title: Choosing a spot
mini_dialogues.situation: You arrive and look for the perfect place to settle.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Where should we set up?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Let's find some shade — it's scorching today.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: There's a lovely clearing near that grove of trees.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Perfect. Spread the picnic rug there.

mini_dialogues.title: Talking about the weather
mini_dialogues.situation: You check the sky during the picnic.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The sky looks a bit overcast.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: There's a cool breeze too — quite pleasant, actually.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: As long as it doesn't drizzle.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Even if it does, we'll just lounge under the umbrella.

mini_dialogues.title: Enjoying the moment
mini_dialogues.situation: You relax and admire the view.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: This is such a laid-back afternoon.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: I know — eating in the open air is the best.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The view across the valley is breathtaking.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Definitely a picture-perfect spot.

mini_dialogues.title: Wrapping up
mini_dialogues.situation: The outing is ending and you pack up.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Should we pack up the leftovers?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Yes, and let's bin the disposable plates.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Want to take a stroll before we head back?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Sure — a little wander along the trail sounds nice. I really needed this change of scenery.

words.english_meaning: Salty or spicy in taste, rather than sweet.
words.usage_note: Opposite of 'sweet'; e.g. samosas are savoury. (US spelling: 'savory'.)
examples: I prefer savoury snacks to sweets.
She made a savoury pie for dinner.
The menu has both sweet and savoury options.
These crackers have a nice savoury flavour.

words.english_meaning: Having little or no strong flavour.
words.usage_note: Negative for taste; food that needs more seasoning.
examples: The soup was bland and needed salt.
Hospital food can be quite bland.
He found the curry too bland.
Add some spices so it isn't bland.

words.english_meaning: Having a strong, sharp, pleasant taste, often sour or citrusy.
words.usage_note: Pleasantly sharp — like lemon, tamarind, or yoghurt.
examples: The tangy lemon dressing was delicious.
I love the tangy taste of tamarind.
The sauce had a nice tangy kick.
Yoghurt gives the dish a tangy flavour.

words.english_meaning: Looking or smelling so delicious that it makes you want to eat it.
words.gujarati_meaning: મોઢામાં પાણી લાવી દે એવું સ્વાદિષ્ટ.
words.usage_note: Strong positive for how food looks or smells.
examples: The mouth-watering smell of biryani filled the house.
The menu had a mouth-watering selection.
She showed me a mouth-watering photo of the cake.
Those sweets look absolutely mouth-watering.

words.english_meaning: (Of food) containing a lot of fat, cream, sugar, or spices; heavy.
words.usage_note: Here 'rich' means heavy/indulgent food, not money.
examples: The chocolate cake was very rich.
This gravy is rich and creamy.
A rich meal can feel heavy.
The dessert was too rich for me.

words.english_meaning: No longer fresh, especially of bread or other food.
words.usage_note: 'Go stale' = become old/dry. Opposite of 'fresh'.
examples: The bread had gone stale.
Don't eat those stale biscuits.
Stale food can upset your stomach.
The cake tasted stale after a week.

words.english_meaning: Having a fresh, lively, often citrus-like flavour.
words.usage_note: Suggests bright, refreshing flavour (often lemon/lime). 'Zest' = citrus peel.
examples: The salad had a zesty lime dressing.
I added orange zest for a zesty taste.
It's a light, zesty summer drink.
The marinade gives the fish a zesty flavour.

words.english_meaning: To cook gently in liquid just below boiling point.
words.usage_note: Slow, gentle cooking with small bubbles, not a rolling boil.
examples: Let the curry simmer for twenty minutes.
Simmer the sauce gently until it thickens.
The soup simmered on the stove.
Reduce the heat and let it simmer.

words.english_meaning: To fry food quickly in a small amount of hot fat or oil.
words.usage_note: Quick frying over high heat. (French; said 'SOH-tay'.)
examples: Sauté the onions until golden.
She sautéed the vegetables in butter.
Lightly sauté the garlic first.
The mushrooms were sautéed to perfection.

words.english_meaning: To soak food in a seasoned liquid before cooking to add flavour.
words.usage_note: The liquid itself is the 'marinade'. Adds flavour and tenderness.
examples: Marinate the chicken overnight for best flavour.
We marinated the paneer in spices.
The meat needs to marinate for an hour.
She marinated the fish in lemon and herbs.

words.english_meaning: To beat eggs, cream, or a mixture quickly to add air.
words.usage_note: Both a verb and the wire tool used for it.
examples: Whisk the eggs until fluffy.
Whisk the batter to remove lumps.
She whisked the cream into soft peaks.
Whisk together the flour and milk.

words.english_meaning: To press and stretch dough with your hands until smooth.
words.usage_note: The 'k' is silent — said 'need'. Essential for bread/roti dough.
examples: Knead the dough for ten minutes.
She kneaded the flour into a soft dough.
Keep kneading until it's smooth.
Well-kneaded dough makes soft rotis.

words.english_meaning: To add salt, pepper, or spices to food to improve its flavour.
words.usage_note: 'Season to taste' = add as much as you like. Noun 'seasoning' = the spices.
examples: Season the soup with salt and pepper.
Don't forget to season the rice.
Season to taste before serving.
She seasoned the curry generously.

words.english_meaning: To decorate food with a small amount of something to make it look attractive.
words.usage_note: Both a verb and a noun (the decoration itself).
examples: Garnish the dish with fresh coriander.
She garnished the soup with cream.
A garnish of lemon adds colour.
The chef garnished the plate with herbs.

words.english_meaning: A style or method of cooking, especially of a particular country or region.
words.usage_note: Refers to a cooking tradition. (French; said 'kwi-ZEEN'.)
examples: I love Italian cuisine.
The restaurant serves South Indian cuisine.
We tried the local cuisine on holiday.
Thai cuisine is known for its bold flavours.

words.english_meaning: A small dish served before the main course to start a meal.
words.gujarati_meaning: મુખ્ય ભોજન પહેલાંની હળવી વાનગી / સ્ટાર્ટર.
words.usage_note: The starter course. (US spelling: 'appetizer'.)
examples: We shared an appetiser before the meal.
The soup was served as an appetiser.
Try the spring rolls as an appetiser.
Appetisers are listed at the top of the menu.

words.english_meaning: The largest or most important dish of a meal.
words.usage_note: Comes after the appetiser and before dessert.
examples: For the main course, I had grilled fish.
The main course was served with rice.
We skipped the main course and went to dessert.
What will you have as a main course?

words.english_meaning: A drink, especially one other than water.
words.usage_note: A formal word for a drink; common on menus.
examples: Would you like a hot beverage?
The menu lists several cold beverages.
Tea is my favourite beverage.
Alcoholic beverages are not served here.

words.english_meaning: A note showing how much you must pay for a meal at a restaurant.
words.usage_note: UK 'the bill', US 'the check'. 'Split the bill' = share the cost.
examples: Could we have the bill, please?
He kindly paid the bill.
Let's split the bill evenly.
The waiter brought the bill to our table.

words.english_meaning: A small extra amount of money given to someone for good service.
words.usage_note: Both noun and verb ('tip the waiter'). Extra money for good service.
examples: We left a generous tip for the waiter.
It's polite to tip for good service.
The service was poor, so we left no tip.
She tipped the driver a little extra.

words.english_meaning: An arrangement to have a table, room, or seat kept for you.
words.usage_note: 'Make/have a reservation' for a table or room.
examples: I made a reservation for two at eight.
Do you have a reservation, sir?
We had to cancel our dinner reservation.
It's wise to book a reservation on weekends.

words.english_meaning: Containing many of the substances the body needs to stay healthy.
words.usage_note: Food that is good for you. Noun: 'nutrition'.
examples: Vegetables are very nutritious.
She cooks nutritious meals for the family.
A nutritious breakfast keeps you energetic.
Fruits are a nutritious snack.

words.english_meaning: Good for your health; healthy and nourishing.
words.usage_note: Suggests simple, natural, healthy food.
examples: They serve wholesome, home-style food.
Oats make a wholesome breakfast.
We prefer wholesome ingredients.
A wholesome diet keeps you fit.

words.english_meaning: An amount of food served to or eaten by one person.
words.gujarati_meaning: એક વ્યક્તિ માટેનો ભોજનનો ભાગ / હિસ્સો.
words.usage_note: 'Portion size' = how much is served. Controlling portions helps health.
examples: The restaurant serves large portions.
Watch your portion sizes.
She gave me a small portion of rice.
Divide the cake into equal portions.

words.english_meaning: To have a very strong desire for a particular food.
words.usage_note: 'Crave' + food; noun 'craving' = a strong urge.
examples: I'm craving something sweet.
She craves spicy food when stressed.
Pregnant women often crave odd foods.
After the gym, I crave a big meal.

words.english_meaning: To eat more food than you need or than is healthy.
words.usage_note: Eating too much; common at feasts/festivals.
examples: It's easy to overeat at a buffet.
I always overeat during festivals.
Try not to overeat before bed.
He overate and felt uncomfortable.

words.english_meaning: A way of eating that includes the right variety and amount of foods for health.
words.usage_note: Includes carbs, protein, fats, and vitamins in proper proportion.
examples: A balanced diet keeps you healthy.
Doctors recommend a balanced diet.
She follows a balanced diet and exercises.
Children need a balanced diet to grow.

words.english_meaning: Extremely hungry.
words.usage_note: A strong word for very hungry (stronger than 'hungry').
examples: I'm famished — let's eat now.
After the hike, we were all famished.
He looked famished and tired.
By lunchtime she was absolutely famished.

words.english_meaning: Slightly hungry.
words.usage_note: Informal British; mildly hungry — wanting a snack.
examples: I'm feeling a bit peckish.
If you're peckish, have some fruit.
We were peckish, so we shared a snack.
A peckish child kept asking for biscuits.

words.english_meaning: The natural desire to eat food.
words.usage_note: 'Lose your appetite' = not feel like eating.
examples: The walk gave me a good appetite.
He has a healthy appetite.
I lost my appetite when I felt ill.
The aroma whetted our appetite.

words.english_meaning: Having eaten enough; not able to eat any more.
words.usage_note: Informal for 'I've eaten enough'.
examples: No more for me, I'm full up.
We were full up after the feast.
I can't finish this — I'm full up.
The kids said they were full up.

words.english_meaning: To eat something by taking small bites.
words.usage_note: Eating slowly in tiny bites; 'nibble on' a snack.
examples: She nibbled on a biscuit.
We nibbled at the snacks while chatting.
The mouse nibbled the cheese.
He nibbled his food without much appetite.

words.english_meaning: To eat something quickly and hungrily.
words.usage_note: Eating fast and eagerly; the opposite of 'nibble'.
examples: The children devoured the pizza.
He devoured his dinner in minutes.
We were so hungry we devoured everything.
She devoured the cake hungrily.

words.english_meaning: A rare or special food that is considered especially nice to eat.
words.usage_note: A prized, often regional special food.
examples: This sweet is a local delicacy.
Fish curry is a delicacy in this region.
We tasted several delicacies on the trip.
Caviar is considered a delicacy.

words.english_meaning: A portion of food given to one person at a meal.
words.usage_note: 'A second helping' = more of the same dish.
examples: Can I have a second helping, please?
She gave me a generous helping of rice.
He took a large helping of dessert.
There's enough for second helpings.

words.english_meaning: Made at home, not bought from a shop.
words.usage_note: Implies fresh, personal cooking. (Also written 'home-made'.)
examples: I love homemade pickles.
The cake was homemade.
Homemade food is healthier.
She brought homemade cookies to share.

words.english_meaning: (Of food or drink) very hot.
words.usage_note: An idiom for freshly cooked, very hot food.
examples: The soup was served piping hot.
Enjoy the rotis piping hot.
She brought out a piping hot pizza.
Nothing beats piping hot tea on a cold day.

words.english_meaning: To eat something quickly, often a small or casual meal.
words.usage_note: Informal — a quick, casual meal.
words.memory_tip: ઝડપથી થોડું ખાઈ લેવું = grab a bite.
examples: Let's grab a bite before the movie.
I only had time to grab a bite.
We grabbed a bite at a roadside stall.
Want to grab a bite after work?

words.english_meaning: To have a meal at a restaurant rather than at home.
words.usage_note: The opposite of 'eat in' / 'cook at home'.
examples: Let's eat out tonight.
We eat out once a week.
They prefer eating out on weekends.
It's cheaper to cook than to eat out.

words.english_meaning: To start eating something eagerly and with enjoyment.
words.usage_note: Informal British; 'tuck into' a meal = eat it heartily.
examples: The food's ready — tuck in!
They tucked into the feast happily.
He tucked into a big plate of biryani.
Don't wait for me; tuck in.

mini_dialogues.situation: Two friends plan dinner.

turns.text: I'm famished. Shall we eat out tonight?

turns.text: Sure! I've been craving some good Italian cuisine.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Let me make a reservation for two.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Great — I could really tuck into a big bowl of pasta.

turns.speaker: Waiter
turns.text: What will you have as a main course?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The grilled fish, please, and a cold beverage.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Shall we order an appetiser to share?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes — and let's remember to leave a tip.

mini_dialogues.title: Cooking at home
mini_dialogues.situation: You praise a friend's home cooking.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: This homemade curry smells mouth-watering!

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Thanks. I let it simmer and seasoned it well.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Did you garnish it with coriander?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Of course. Tuck in while it's piping hot!

mini_dialogues.title: Eating healthily
mini_dialogues.situation: Talking about diet.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I'm trying to follow a balanced diet.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Good idea — eat more nutritious, wholesome food.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: But I still crave sweets sometimes.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: A small portion now and then is fine.

mini_dialogues.title: A snack break
mini_dialogues.situation: Offering a snack before dinner.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Are you hungry?

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Just a little peckish, actually.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: There are some biscuits — nibble on those for now.

turns.speaker: Friend
turns.text: Thanks. I don't want to overeat before dinner.
